text:
**A 200-300 W solar setup is the practical answer for a 1,000 Wh power station.** 200 W refills it in about a day and a half of decent sun, and about 300 W does it in one good summer day.

**The formula**

Panel watts ≈ 1,000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses, since panels rarely deliver their rated watts ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).

**Panel watts to fully recharge 1,000 Wh in one day** ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/))

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts needed |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter or cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer, Southwest) | ~230 W |

**Smaller panels take longer, at 4.5 peak sun hours and 70% efficiency** ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/))
- 100 W gives about 315 Wh a day, so roughly 3 days.
- 200 W gives about 630 Wh a day, so roughly 1.5 days.
- 400 W gives about 1,260 Wh a day, so under a day.

Another guide puts a northern-winter recharge at 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Check these before buying**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many solar watts it accepts, often 200-800 W for 1,000 Wh class units. Panels beyond that add nothing in good sun ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- **Voltage window:** The panels' open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input range. Wiring panels in series adds voltage and can damage the station if it goes over ([SolarNiverse](https://solarniverse.com/chargers/charge-power-station-with-solar-panels/)).
- **Using the station while charging:** Any power you draw during the day slows the recharge.

**If you want a single 400 W panel**
